rawText: Ss eS SS SS Se —— as es Ss ee JAMES HENRY and PEARL C. FRANCIS A SON’S TRIBUTE James Henry Francis, and his sister, Ella, were born to Josephine Francis Scott in a single-parent household. During his early childhood and after his mother’s marriage to Mr. William Scott, Father James and his sister Ella were sent to live with their grandmother. At this early age, Father was entrusted into the awful responsibility of becoming the man of the household. This meant tilling a small acreage of land with an ox, and caring for his ailing grandmother. Even with an ailing grandmother and a sister to care for, he and his sister attended the public school on a somewhat regular basis, and completed a curriculum that would parallel the eighth grade today. They both joined the church and became supportive members. Upon the death of their grandmother, Aunt Ella married Mr. James Davis, and Father James chose the young lady of his heart, Miss Pearl Martha Ann Clanton | whose family background could be seen closely paralleling that of his own. The difference being, her family “4 consisted of four sisters: Aunt Hatty, Mary, Josie, and Sally Ann, and one brother, Jimmy as well as her mother, Nancy Roberson. Uncle Jimmy and Aunt Sally Ann became very prosperous landowners in their own right. Immediately after marriage, Father and Mother launched into two enterprises that proved rather courageous and adventurous. They invested their somewhat limited resources in a community grocery store, while at the same time began rearing a family. Their merchandizing business prospered to the extent that they were able to enjoy the distinction of owning a horse and a buggy. A rare status symbol to be enjoyed by such a newlywed couple in those days. The skill and determination with which this young couple managed their family and business caught the eyes and won the respect of several community leaders and landowners.
